Piriformis syndrome is commonly mistaken for herniated disc in the low back, since they have a lot of similar pain patterns. 
.
➡️ What’s different about pirifomis syndrome, though, is that it’s a muscle issue (and not a spinal joint problem). 
.
It occurs when the piriformis muscle (which lies deep to the glute or buttock) spasms and irritates the sciatic nerve. ⚡️⚡️
.
Symptoms usually include tenderness and pain in the buttock area, and possible sciatica like shooting pains, numbness, and weakness in the leg.  
.
➡️ Long periods of sitting or driving tend to be a main trigger for piriformis issues. Strenuous exercise and unresolved sacroiliac joint, hip, or spinal injuries can also put strain on this muscle. 
.
So if there's a lot of pain while walking up stairs, sitting, or running… there’s a chance it could be a piriformis issue. 
.
Watch the video, do the test, and see if it helps answer some questions!
